 John Christ, Original Danzig Guitarist on ‘Mother’ and More, Dead at 61
 The musician was part of the band’s original lineup and helped shaped its distinct sound in the Nineties

 Charisma Madarang

 John Christ, the guitarist behind the original lineup of metal band Danzig , died on Sunday. He was 61.
 His death was confirmed on his website. “Friends, It is with a heavy heart that we must inform you of the peaceful passing of John Christ on November 15, 2026,” read the statement. “No services are planned and we kindly ask everyone to respect the family’s privacy during this time. John loved each and every one of you.” A cause of death was not immediately available.
 The musician, born John Wolfgang Knoll, had previously shared an update with fans about his health in early September. Christ said that he had been focusing on a “medical issue that has been kicking my butt” and doctors requested that he take a few months off to recuperate. Christ, who taught private lessons and held workshops, said that he was stepping about from teaching and live gigs until further notice. 
 In 1987, Christ joined the goth-punk band Samhain, led by Misfits founder Glenn Danzig, which would later become Danzig. Christ later recalled auditioning for the part in front of Danzig and Rick Rubin, who was on the look for bands to sign to his record label, Def Jam Recording. “We were jamming at a furious pace. Samhain used only downstrokes with no alternate picking,” Christ said. “At some point, I tore the fingernail off my index finger, and it began to bleed everywhere. I accidentally brushed up against Glenn and left six bloody lines on his shoulder. Rick Rubin thought this was awesome. Glenn thought I was on speed. I was just pissed off because I had to wait four hours to audition.”
 As the story goes, it wasn’t until Christ left a slew of guitar solos on Danzig’s answering machine that he was finally invited to join the crew.
 As part of Danzig’s original lineup, Christ’s work helped shaped the band’s identity and his bluesy, riff-oriented guitar can be heard on across four studio albums Danzig (1988), Danzig II: Lucifuge (1990), Danzig III: How the Gods Kill (1992), Danzig 4P (1994) and the 1993 EP Thrall-Demonsweatlive . During this period, that band earned gold records for Danzig and Thrall-Demonsweatlive , and released their 1993 hit “Mother,” embarking on numerous U.S. and international tours alongside Metallica, Black Sabbath, Slayer, and more.

 Christ also featured on Live on the Black Hand Side (2001) and The Lost Tracks of Danzig (2007). He left Danzig in 1995. When looking back at that time during a 2018 interview with Metal Inside r, Christ said, “That was a magical time that we were together and doing it that way for as long as we did,” adding, “I just look back and wish that we’d all been more mature. Myself especially. I’d like to entertain the thought that had I been a better communicator we could have hung in there a bit longer and mended some of those fences at the time. I didn’t know how to do that and I didn’t know what to say.”
 The musician released his only solo record, Flesh Caffeine , in 1999. “I was actually having fun writing songs again,” Christ told Guitar World in 2021. “Prior to that, it seems like every note had a dollar value associated with it. Now that I had freedom, I said, ‘Let it rip, no expectations,’ and I experimented with drop D tuning for the first time ever and fell in love.”
